title: Finite etale-local splitting descends through a surjective closed immersion
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], let $r:R\to Y$ be a surjective closed immersion [def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $U\subseteq Y$ be open. Put $U_R=r^{-1}(U)$ and $g:X\times_Y R\to R$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume an etale covering family $T_i\to U_R$ is given such that each $T_i\times_{U_R} g^{-1}(U_R)$ has a finite pairwise disjoint open covering $(W_{ij})_{j\in\operatorname{Fin}(n_i)}$, and each composite $W_{ij}\to T_i$ is a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. Then there is an etale covering family $S_a\to U$ such that every $S_a\times_U f^{-1}(U)$ likewise has a finite pairwise disjoint open covering whose component maps to $S_a$ are universal homeomorphisms. The integers may be zero. There are no Noetherian, reduced, affine or density assumptions.

source.document: Stacks Project, etale-cohomology.tex and morphisms.tex; parent generic finite Noetherian splitting proof

proof.text: Restrict r to U. It remains a surjective closed immersion, hence a universal homeomorphism. Apply the equivalence of small etale sites to each object of the given etale cover to lift it to an etale scheme over U. The lifted objects cover U because base change along a universal homeomorphism reflects jointly surjective families.

For each lifted cover T, base change the finite source to T. Its base change to the old cover is identified with the old source by associativity of fibre products. The vertical map is a surjective closed immersion and a homeomorphism. Let the new W_j be the images of the old W_j under this homeomorphism. The images are open, pairwise disjoint and cover. Each W_j is clopen: its complement is the union of the finitely many other opens. Consequently W_j -> P is a closed immersion as well as an open immersion; it is finite, and W_j -> T is finite by composition.

After any base change T_prime -> T, the old cover maps bijectively onto the new cover, and the old source maps bijectively onto the new source, since the two vertical arrows are base changes of a surjective closed immersion. The old W_j pulls back to the inverse image of the new W_j, so their vertical map is bijective too. The old component map is bijective after this base change by its universal-homeomorphism hypothesis. The commutative square with bijective vertical arrows then implies that the new W_j -> T_prime is bijective. Thus the new W_j -> T is universally injective and surjective. Its finiteness from the previous step implies integrality, giving precisely IsUniversalHomeomorphism. The argument applies also to n=0 (the old and new sources are then empty), and an empty base is covered by the empty family.

theorem finite_splitting_descends_surjective_closedImmersion
    {X Y R : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f]
    (r : R ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion r] [Surjective r] (U : Y.Opens)
    (h : ∃ 𝒯 : Cover.{u} etalePrecoverage (r ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme, ∀ i,
      ∃ (n : ℕ)
        (W : Fin n → (pullback (𝒯.f i) (pullback.snd f r ∣_ (r ⁻¹ᵁ U))).Opens),
        (⨆ j, W j) = ⊤ ∧ Pairwise (fun j k ↦ Disjoint (W j) (W k)) ∧
        ∀ j, IsUniversalHomeomorphism
          ((W j).ι ≫ pullback.fst (𝒯.f i) (pullback.snd f r ∣_ (r ⁻¹ᵁ U)))) :
    ∃ 𝒯 : Cover.{u} etalePrecoverage U.toScheme, ∀ i,
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (W : Fin n → (pullback (𝒯.f i) (f ∣_ U)).Opens),
        (⨆ j, W j) = ⊤ ∧ Pairwise (fun j k ↦ Disjoint (W j) (W k)) ∧
        ∀ j, IsUniversalHomeomorphism
          ((W j).ι ≫ pullback.fst (𝒯.f i) (f ∣_ U))
